text:
ConocoPhillips stock fell 3.6% today to $134.40, wiping out most of its gains from the past week. The drop came as crude oil prices retreated—U.S. oil fell below $90 per barrel—despite escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. This suggests that whatever risk premium investors were paying for Iranian threats and Strait of Hormuz disruptions a day or two ago has worn off, and profit-taking is outweighing the safety bid that typically supports energy stocks during regional crises.

The broader context is that oil majors like ConocoPhillips have been trading on a knife's edge: geopolitical scares push prices up temporarily, but then recede as markets decide the actual supply disruption won't materialize or is already priced in. The IEA's warning that confidence in the Strait—one of the world's critical chokepoints—has been "crushed" should theoretically support prices, but falling prices suggest the market is skeptical of near-term supply loss, allowing the stock to give back recent gains.
